bug_semantics: The login endpoint accepts an attacker-controlled `url` parameter and checks it with URL parsing/host logic that does not recognize a leading backslash as an external host. The value then reaches `goto_url()`, which emits it in an HTTP `Location` header (or equivalent script/meta redirect). A request such as `bbs/login.php?url=\google.com` therefore passes the same-host check but is interpreted by the client as an attacker-selected redirect, enabling phishing and exposure of information through the redirect flow.
flaw_origin: Repository commit 41d21074b5fcf579633c255f3b499434b2d4d46b first added both sides of the flawed mechanism: `bbs/login.php` read `$_GET['url']`, accepted values for which `parse_url()` exposed neither a disallowed scheme nor host, and passed the unchecked value to `goto_url()`; `lib/common.lib.php` implemented `goto_url()` by placing the value directly in `Location`, JavaScript, or meta-refresh output. The immediate parent contains neither file. Later revisions replaced the inline `parse_url()` check with `check_url_host()` but retained the same backslash blind spot through the vendor-confirmed affected v5.5.16 tag.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object identifies author and committer as `kagla` (display name `gnuboard`), has the sole commit message `그누보드5`, an empty body, and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot, Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, or other AI attribution marker.
evidence: The first-party report https://github.com/gnuboard/gnuboard5/issues/320 identifies Open Redirect in version 5.5.16, names `bbs/login.php`, states that the `url` parameter lacks backslash filtering, and supplies the PoCs `https://demo.sir.kr/gnuboard5/bbs/login.php?url=\google.com` and `...?url=\github.com`.

At the affected tag, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gnuboard/gnuboard5/v5.5.16/bbs/login.php shows the vulnerable path at `bbs/login.php` lines 11-21: `$url` is copied from `$_GET['url']`, `check_url_host($url)` is called, and an already-authenticated request passes `$url` to `goto_url($url)`. The tag history at https://github.com/gnuboard/gnuboard5/commits/v5.5.16 resolves the affected release tip to 02e0996eb4293c8edd9aea807f9282cdb5c6d9f3.

The BIC source at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gnuboard/gnuboard5/41d21074b5fcf579633c255f3b499434b2d4d46b/bbs/login.php first writes the vulnerable route at lines 7-20: it reads `$_GET['url']`, rejects only a parsed foreign scheme/host, then calls `goto_url($url)`. The same BIC's `lib/common.lib.php` lines 84-97, visible at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gnuboard/gnuboard5/41d21074b5fcf579633c255f3b499434b2d4d46b/lib/common.lib.php, writes the unfiltered redirect sink (`header('Location: '.$url)` plus script/meta fallbacks). Commit: https://github.com/gnuboard/gnuboard5/commit/41d21074b5fcf579633c255f3b499434b2d4d46b.

The BIC commit object names direct parent 04c3efa279d60f646bf3b430750ab5a98fcc6eef. Direct parent-tree verification found both vulnerable files absent: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gnuboard/gnuboard5/04c3efa279d60f646bf3b430750ab5a98fcc6eef/bbs/login.php and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gnuboard/gnuboard5/04c3efa279d60f646bf3b430750ab5a98fcc6eef/lib/common.lib.php each return HTTP 404. Thus the vulnerable route and sink are absent from the immediate parent, rather than merely moved or refactored.

Direct fix https://github.com/gnuboard/gnuboard5/commit/e03e01d41098f6a42788e53cb8bd5894ce47cd15 adds `safe_filter_url_host()` and applies it at `goto_url()` and related redirect sinks. The helper derives a backslash regex and removes every backslash before the redirect is emitted. Its parent 940e701fa460785f6cbf5cec5dbe60faf1df7f8b lacks that filtering, so e03e01d41098f6a42788e53cb8bd5894ce47cd15 is the first effective sink fix for the reported payload.

The vendor security notice https://sir.kr/g5_pds/7205 and release page https://github.com/gnuboard/gnuboard5/releases/tag/v5.5.17 identify v5.5.17 as the security-patch release, link the Open Redirect fix e03e01d41098f6a42788e53cb8bd5894ce47cd15, and place it before the v5.5.17 release/version commit 8c505f6f1da4a8a63b32e9c6d1fa906e738cb4d2. The tag history https://github.com/gnuboard/gnuboard5/commits/v5.5.17 contains e03e01d and resolves the fixed release tip to 8c505f6f1da4a8a63b32e9c6d1fa906e738cb4d2, establishing affected v5.5.16 and fixed v5.5.17 boundaries.

A later defense-in-depth commit, https://github.com/gnuboard/gnuboard5/commit/c6b58bb16b27cba0dceebf6bfcddd95093132ddf, removes the local `bbs/login.php` reassignment and changes `common.php` request sanitization to an allowlist that excludes backslash. This later hardening does not change the earliest fixed boundary because v5.5.17 already contains the sink-level backslash removal in e03e01d41098f6a42788e53cb8bd5894ce47cd15.

History shows that the smallest public-repository commit writing this causal source/check/sink combination is 41d21074b5fcf579633c255f3b499434b2d4d46b; both implicated files are missing from its direct parent's tree, so this is not a blame artifact, move, or later refactor.
